title: Conditional Types, infer & Template Literal Types
description: Master advanced type-level programming: conditional types with T extends U ? X : Y, the infer keyword for type extraction, distributive conditionals, and template literal types for string-based type manipulation.

data.text: TypeScript conditional types (`T extends U ? X : Y`) bring if-then-else logic to the type system. Unlike simple type aliases, conditional types can examine the shape of an input type and branch to different output types. This enables building utility types that automatically adapt their output based on the input type's structure—a critical capability when typing complex AI streaming event systems, MCP tool call payloads, or agent action discriminants.

data.title: Conditional Type: Unwrap Async or Sync Values Uniformly
data.content: A universal Awaited-like type that unwraps any level of Promise nesting.

data.text: The infer Keyword: Extracting Types from Type Patterns

`infer` can only appear inside the `extends` clause of a conditional type. It introduces a type variable that TypeScript infers from the matched structure—like pattern matching in functional languages.

data.title: Extracting Types from Function and Tuple Structures
data.content: Using infer to extract argument types from event handler signatures without importing them.

data.text: When a generic conditional type receives a union type as its parameter, TypeScript automatically distributes the condition over each member of the union. This powers many of the built-in utility types like `Exclude` and `Extract`.

data.title: Distributive Conditional for Nullable Stripping
data.content: Creating a NonNullableDeep utility that recursively removes null/undefined from nested types.

data.text: Template Literal Types: String Pattern Types
Template literal types construct string types by combining string unions. They are invaluable for typing event names, CSS class patterns, API route paths, and SSE event type identifiers.

data.title: Type-Safe SSE Event Namespacing with Template Literals
data.content: Automatically deriving all valid namespaced event type strings from union components.

data.title: Conditional & Template Literal Types Mastery
items: Use conditional types with infer to extract nested types without importing private SDK types
Wrap type parameter in tuple [T] to disable distribution when testing entire unions
Use template literal types to construct exhaustive string union types for events and routes
Test conditional type edge cases with @ts-expect-error to verify compile-time errors
Use recursive conditional types to unwrap arbitrarily nested Promises or arrays
Avoid overly complex conditional type chains that degrade TypeScript compilation performance

data.title: Summary & Next Steps
points: Conditional types enable if-then-else logic at the type level using T extends U ? X : Y.
The infer keyword extracts type information from matching structures inside conditional types.
Distributive conditionals automatically map over union types for type filtering.
Template literal types generate exhaustive string union types for events, routes, and namespaces.
data.takeaway: Conditional types and template literals elevate TypeScript from a type annotator to a full type-level programming language—enabling APIs that are self-validating at compile time.
